rows.stem: A few pieces of granulated zinc are taken in a test tube and 2 mL of sodium hydroxide solution is added to it. When the contents are warmed, the product formed is :

options.label: A
options.text: \(\mathrm{Na_2ZnO}\)

options.label: B
options.text: \(\mathrm{NaZnO_2}\)

options.label: C
options.text: \(\mathrm{Na_2ZnO_2}\)

options.label: D
options.text: \(\mathrm{NaZn(OH)_2}\)

rows.solution:
Zinc reacts with sodium hydroxide solution on warming to form sodium zincate, and hydrogen gas is given off:

\(\mathrm{2NaOH + Zn \rightarrow Na_2ZnO_2 + H_2}\)

This is option (C) \(\mathrm{Na_2ZnO_2}\).

rows.stem: The essential element used in the synthesis of proteins is :

options.label: A
options.text: Nitrogen

options.label: B
options.text: Phosphorus

options.label: C
options.text: Iron

options.label: D
options.text: Magnesium

rows.solution: Proteins contain nitrogen, which plants take up from the soil as inorganic nitrates or nitrites and use to make their proteins and other compounds. This is option (A) Nitrogen.

rows.stem: Which one of the following statements is **not** correct for the plants raised by vegetative propagation ?

options.label: A
options.text: Can bear flowers and fruits earlier than those produced from seeds.

options.label: B
options.text: Those plants that have lost the capacity to produce seeds can be grown.

options.label: C
options.text: As compared to the parent plant, vegetatively propagated plants show more variations.

options.label: D
options.text: All the plants produced in this way are genetically similar to the parent plant.

rows.solution:
A vegetatively propagated plant comes from a part of a single parent, with no fusion of gametes, so it is genetically similar to the parent and shows hardly any variation. The other three statements are true: such plants flower and fruit earlier, and plants that have lost the capacity to produce seeds (banana, orange, rose, jasmine) can still be grown this way.

The statement that is not correct is option (C) As compared to the parent plant, vegetatively propagated plants show more variations.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: In the human eye, most of the refraction for the light rays entering the eye occurs at the surface of :

options.label: A
options.text: Cornea

options.label: B
options.text: Crystalline lens

options.label: C
options.text: Pupil

options.label: D
options.text: Aqueous humor

rows.solution:
Most of the refraction of the light entering the eye occurs at the outer surface of the cornea. The crystalline lens only fine-tunes the focal length to focus objects at different distances on the retina.

This is option (A) Cornea.

rows.stem: The resistivity of a wire made of an alloy is generally :

options.label: A
options.text: Lower than that of its constituent metals.

options.label: B
options.text: Higher than that of its constituent metals.

options.label: C
options.text: Decreases with increase in its area of cross-section.

options.label: D
options.text: Increases with increase in its length.

rows.solution:
The resistivity of an alloy is generally higher than that of its constituent metals, which is why alloys such as nichrome are used in heating devices. Resistivity depends only on the material (and temperature), not on the length or the area of cross-section of the wire, so the last two choices describe resistance, not resistivity.

This is option (B) Higher than that of its constituent metals.

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Propanal and propanone are structural isomers.

**Reason (R) :** Propanal and propanone both have the same molecular formula.
rows.context: For Questions number 17 to 20, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Propanal, \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CHO}\), and propanone, \(\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}\), have the same molecular formula, \(\mathrm{C_3H_6O}\), but different structures: one has an aldehyde group and the other a ketone group. Compounds with the same molecular formula and different structures are structural isomers, so the Assertion is true.

The Reason is true, and it is exactly why the two compounds are isomers, so it is the correct explanation of the Assertion.

This is option (A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

rows.stem:
Balance the following chemical equations :

(a) \(\mathrm{CO_2 + H_2O \xrightarrow[\text{Chlorophyll}]{\text{Sunlight}} C_6H_{12}O_6 + O_2 + H_2O}\)

(b) \(\mathrm{Pb(NO_3)_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Heat}} PbO + NO_2 + O_2}\)
rows.solution:
(a) Six carbon atoms in glucose need 6 \(\mathrm{CO_2}\). Glucose has 12 hydrogen atoms and the product water 2 more per molecule, so with 6 \(\mathrm{H_2O}\) on the right there are 24 hydrogen atoms there, which needs 12 \(\mathrm{H_2O}\) on the left. Oxygen then balances with 6 \(\mathrm{O_2}\) (24 atoms on each side):

\(\mathrm{6CO_2 + 12H_2O \xrightarrow[\text{Chlorophyll}]{\text{Sunlight}} C_6H_{12}O_6 + 6O_2 + 6H_2O}\)

(b) Two molecules of lead nitrate give 2 PbO and 4 \(\mathrm{NO_2}\); the 12 oxygen atoms on the left leave 2 for one \(\mathrm{O_2}\):

\(\mathrm{2Pb(NO_3)_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Heat}} 2PbO + 4NO_2 + O_2}\)

rows.stem:
Study the given diagram and write the type of movement exhibited by :

(a) Root, and

(b) Shoot,

mentioning the stimulus in each case.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - a line drawing of a potted plant with the pot tipped over onto its side; roots come out of one end of the pot and the leafy shoot out of the other. The directions in which the root and the shoot grow, which the question tests, are shown only in the drawing and are withheld here. Page idx 12.
rows.solution:
In the drawing the pot is tipped on its side, yet the roots have grown downwards and the shoot has bent upwards.

(a) Root: it grows downwards, towards the pull of the earth, so it shows positive geotropism. Stimulus: gravity.

(b) Shoot: it grows upwards, away from the pull of the earth, so it shows negative geotropism. Stimulus: gravity.

(The movements can also be read as a response to light: the shoot bending towards light is positive phototropism, and the root growing away from light is negative phototropism, with light as the stimulus. The marking scheme accepts either.)

rows.stem: An electric fuse is rated 8 A. Can it be used with an electrical appliance of rating 5 kW, 200 V ? Justify your answer.
rows.solution:
The current drawn by the appliance is

\(I = \dfrac{P}{V} = \dfrac{5000\ \text{W}}{200\ \text{V}} = 25\) A.

No, the fuse cannot be used. The appliance draws 25 A, far more than the 8 A rating of the fuse, so the fuse wire would melt as soon as the appliance is switched on, breaking the circuit, and the appliance would stop working.

rows.stem:
Study the experimental set-up given in the figure and answer the following questions :

(a) Identify these metals from the following which can be used as “metal sample” in the given set-up :

Aluminium, Copper, Iron, Lead, Silver

(b) Write balanced chemical equations for the reaction in each case.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - a laboratory set-up: a horizontal tube clamped to a stand holds glass-wool soaked in water at its closed end and a coiled metal sample, heated by a burner; a cork carries a delivery tube down into a trough of water, where the gas bubbles into an inverted, water-filled jar labelled 'Hydrogen gas', held by a second stand. The stem never says the metal reacts with steam; only the drawing shows it. Page idx 14.
rows.solution:
The set-up passes steam over the heated metal and collects hydrogen gas over water, so the metal must react with steam.

(a) Of the metals listed, aluminium and iron react with steam. Lead, copper and silver do not react with water at all.

(b) Each forms its oxide and hydrogen:

\(\mathrm{2Al(s) + 3H_2O(g) \rightarrow Al_2O_3(s) + 3H_2(g)}\)

\(\mathrm{3Fe(s) + 4H_2O(g) \rightarrow Fe_3O_4(s) + 4H_2(g)}\)

rows.stem:
(a) What is meant by reflex arc ? Where are they formed in the human body ?

(b) Why have reflex arcs evolved in animals ?
rows.solution:
(a) A reflex arc is the pathway followed by a nerve impulse during a reflex action: the connection that detects the input and quickly responds to it with an output action. It runs from the receptor (for example heat or pain receptors in the skin) along a sensory neuron to the spinal cord, through a relay neuron, and back along a motor neuron to the effector (for example a muscle in the arm), while a message also goes on to the brain.

Reflex arcs are formed in the spinal cord.

(b) Reflex arcs have evolved because the thinking process of the brain is not fast enough. In an emergency (touching a hot object) the response must be immediate, and the brain would take longer to respond, so the spinal cord produces the response directly.

rows.subtopic: Lens Formula and Power of a Lens
rows.stem: An object is placed at a distance of 20 cm from the optical centre of a concave lens and its image is formed on the same side of the lens as the object. If the distance of the image from optical centre of the lens is 10 cm, use lens formula to determine (i) focal length, and (ii) power of the lens in new Cartesian sign conventions.
rows.solution:
For a concave lens with the image on the same side as the object, both distances are negative: \(u = -20\) cm, \(v = -10\) cm.

(i) By the lens formula,

\(\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{-10} - \dfrac{1}{-20} = -\dfrac{1}{10} + \dfrac{1}{20} = \dfrac{-2 + 1}{20} = -\dfrac{1}{20}\)

so \(f = -20\) cm.

(ii) With the focal length in metres, \(f = -0{\cdot}2\) m:

\(P = \dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{-0{\cdot}2} = -5\) D.

The negative signs show that the lens is diverging (concave).

rows.stem:
Resistance of a wire of length 1 m is \(35\,\Omega\) at 20°C. If the diameter of the wire is \(0{\cdot}2\) mm, determine the resistivity of the material of the wire at that temperature. How will the resistivity of the wire change if the length and diameter of the wire both are doubled ? Justify your answer.

(Given that \(\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}\))
rows.solution:
\(R = 35\,\Omega\), \(l = 1\) m and diameter \(2r = 0{\cdot}2\) mm \(= 2 \times 10^{-4}\) m, so \(r = 10^{-4}\) m.

Area of cross-section: \(A = \pi r^2 = \dfrac{22}{7} \times (10^{-4})^2 = \dfrac{22}{7} \times 10^{-8}\ \text{m}^2\).

From \(R = \rho \dfrac{l}{A}\),

\(\rho = \dfrac{RA}{l} = \dfrac{35 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 10^{-8}}{1} = 110 \times 10^{-8}\,\Omega\,\text{m} = 1{\cdot}1 \times 10^{-6}\,\Omega\,\text{m}\)

The resistivity will not change when the length and diameter are doubled. Resistivity is a characteristic property of the material (at a given temperature) and does not depend on the dimensions of the wire. (The resistance changes: doubling the length doubles it and doubling the diameter makes the area four times as large, so the resistance becomes half, but the resistivity stays \(1{\cdot}1 \times 10^{-6}\,\Omega\,\text{m}\).)
